plan: 2 Samuel 2:1-7, 8-11, 12-17, 18–3:1; 2 Samuel 3:2-5; 1 Chronicles 3:1-4a; 2 Samuel 23:8-17; 1 Chronicles 11:10-19; 2 Samuel 23:18-39; 1 Chronicles 11:20-47

readings.title: The Expansion of the Rightful Authority
readings.subtitle: The Incremental Growth of Daviḏ's House
readings.text: [2 Samuel 3:1] And the fighting between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Daviḏ was long drawn out. But Daviḏ was going on and was strong, and the house of Sha’ul was going on and was weak. [2] And sons were born to Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron. And his first-born was Amnon by Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess; [3] and his second, Kil’aḇ, by Aḇiġayil the widow of Naḇal the Karmelite; and the third, Aḇshalom son of Ma’aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, sovereign of Geshur; [4] and the fourth, Aḏoniyah son of Ḥaggith; and the fifth, Shephatyah son of Aḇital; [5] and the sixth, Yithre’am, by Daviḏ’s wife Eġlah. These were born to Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron.

readings.title: Friction in the Adversarial House
readings.subtitle: The Internal Collapse of Sha’ul's Dynasty
readings.text: [6] And it came to be, while there was fighting between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Daviḏ, that Aḇnĕr was strengthening himself in the house of Sha’ul. [7] And Sha’ul had a concubine, whose name was Ritspah, daughter of Ayah. And Ishbosheth said to Aḇnĕr, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?” [8] And Aḇnĕr was very displeased at the words of Ishbosheth, and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Yehuḏah, that I show loving-commitment to the house of Sha’ul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends today, and have not let you fall into the hand of Daviḏ, that you charge me today with a sin concerning this woman? [9] “<dn>Elohim</dn> does so to Aḇnĕr, and more also, if I do not do for Daviḏ as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn to him: [10] to cause the reign to pass over from the house of Sha’ul, and to raise up <dn>את</dn> the throne of Daviḏ over Yisra’ĕl and over Yehuḏah, from Dan to Be’ĕrsheḇa.” [11] And he was unable to answer <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr another word, because he feared him.

readings.title: The Covenant of Unity
readings.subtitle: The Right Arm Gathers the Tribes
readings.text: [12] And Aḇnĕr sent messengers on his behalf to Daviḏ, saying, “Whose is the land?” saying also, “Make your covenant with <dn>את</dn> me, and see, my hand is with <dn>את</dn> you to bring <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl to you.” [13] And Daviḏ said, “Good, I make a covenant with <dn>את</dn> you. Only one matter I am asking of you: you do not see <dn>את</dn> my face unless you first bring <dn>את</dn> Miḵal, daughter of Sha’ul, when you come to see <dn>את</dn> my face.” [14] Daviḏ then sent messengers to Ishbosheth son of Sha’ul, saying, “Give me <dn>את</dn> my wife <dn>את</dn> Miḵal, to whom I became engaged for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.” [15] And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Palti’ĕl son of Layish. [16] But her husband went with <dn>את</dn> her to Baḥurim, going on and weeping behind her. And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Go, turn back!” And he turned back. [17] And Aḇnĕr had a word with the elders of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “In time past you were seeking for Daviḏ to be sovereign over you. [18] “And now, do it! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken of Daviḏ, saying, <dq>‘By the hand of <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ, <dn>I</dn> save <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl from the hand of the Philistines and the hand of all their enemies.’</dq> ” [19] And Aḇnĕr also spoke in the hearing of Binyamin. And Aḇnĕr also went to speak in the hearing of Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron <dn>את</dn> all that seemed good to Yisra’ĕl and all the house of Binyamin. [20] And Aḇnĕr and twenty men with <dn>את</dn> him came to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron. And Daviḏ made a feast for Aḇnĕr and the men who were with <dn>את</dn> him. [21] And Aḇnĕr said to Daviḏ, “Let me arise and go, and gather <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl to my master the sovereign, and let them make a covenant with <dn>את</dn> you, and you shall reign over all that your being desires.” And Daviḏ sent <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr away, and he went in peace.

readings.title: The Retributive Spirit
readings.subtitle: Yo’aḇ's Unrighteous Extraction
readings.text: [22] And see, the servants of Daviḏ and Yo’aḇ came from a raid and brought much spoil with <dn>את</dn> them. But Aḇnĕr was not with <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ in Ḥeḇron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace. [23] And Yo’aḇ and all the army that was with <dn>את</dn> him came, and they reported to Yo’aḇ, saying, “Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to the sovereign, and he sent him away, and he has gone in peace.” [24] And Yo’aḇ went to the sovereign and said, “What have you done? See, Aḇnĕr has come to you! Why is it that you sent him away, and he has already gone? [25] “You know <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to deceive you, to know <dn>את</dn> your going out and <dn>את</dn> your coming in, and to know <dn>את</dn> all that you are doing.” [26] Yo’aḇ then left Daviḏ, and he sent messengers after Aḇnĕr, who brought <dn>את</dn> him back from the well of Sirah. But Daviḏ did not know it. [27] Thus Aḇnĕr returned to Ḥeḇron, and Yo’aḇ took him aside in the gate to speak with <dn>את</dn> him privately, and there struck him in the stomach, so that he died for the blood of Asah’ĕl his brother. [28] And when Daviḏ heard it afterwards, he said, “My reign and I are guiltless before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever of the blood of Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [29] “Let it rest on the head of Yo’aḇ and on all his father’s house. And let there never fail to be in the house of Yo’aḇ one who has a discharge or is a leper, or who is taking hold of a staff or falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.” [30] So Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother killed Aḇnĕr, because he had killed <dn>את</dn> their brother <dn>את</dn> Asah’ĕl at Giḇ’on in the battle.

readings.title: Premial Leadership
readings.subtitle: A Sovereign's Refusal to Embrace the Penal Way
readings.text: [31] And Daviḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to all the people who were with <dn>את</dn> him, “Tear your garments, gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn for Aḇnĕr.” And Sovereign Daviḏ followed the coffin. [32] And they buried <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron. And the sovereign lifted up <dn>את</dn> his voice and wept at the burial-site of Aḇnĕr, and all the people wept. [33] And the sovereign sang a lament over Aḇnĕr and said, “Should Aḇnĕr die as a fool dies? [34] “Your hands were not bound nor your feet put into shackles. As one falls before sons of evil, so you fell.” And all the people wept over him again. [35] And all the people came to cause <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ to eat food while it was still day, but Daviḏ swore, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or whatever else till the sun goes down!” [36] And all the people took note of it, and it was good in their eyes, since whatever the sovereign did was good in the eyes of all the people. [37] And all the people and all Yisra’ĕl knew that day that it had not been the sovereign’s intent to kill <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [38] The sovereign also said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great one has fallen in Yisra’ĕl today? [39] “And I am weak today, though anointed sovereign. And these men, the sons of Tseruyah, are too harsh for me. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> repay the evil-doer according to his evil.”

readings.title: The Geometric Expansion of the King's House
readings.subtitle: The Foundation of the Royal Lineage
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 3:1] And these were the sons of Daviḏ who were born to him in Ḥeḇron: The first-born was Amnon, by Aḥino’am the Yizre’ĕlitess; the second, Dani’ĕl, by Aḇiġayil the Karmelitess; [2] the third, Aḇshalom son of Ma’aḵah, the daughter of Talmai, sovereign of Geshur; the fourth, Aḏoniyah son of Ḥaggith; [3] the fifth, Shephatyah, by Aḇital; the sixth, Yithre’am, by his wife Eġlah. [4] Six were born to him in Ḥeḇron. And he reigned there seven years and six new moons, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years. [5] And these were born to him in Yerushalayim: Shim’a, and Shoḇaḇ, and Nathan, and Shelomoh – four by Bathshua the daughter of Ammi’ĕl. [6] Yiḇḥar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet, [7] and Noġah, and Nepheġ, and Yaphiya, [8] and Elishama, and Elyaḏa, and Eliphelet, nine, [9] all the sons of Daviḏ, besides the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.

readings.title: The Decreed Chain of Kings
readings.subtitle: From Shelomoh to the Bavel Captivity
readings.text: [10] And Shelomoh’s son was Reḥaḇ’am, Aḇiyah his son, Asa his son, Yehoshaphat his son, [11] Yoram his son, Aḥazyahu his son, Yo’ash his son, [12] Amatsyahu his son, Azaryah his son, Yotham his son, [13] Aḥaz his son, Ḥizqiyahu his son, Menashsheh his son, [14] Amon his son, Yoshiyahu his son. [15] And the sons of Yoshiyahu: Yoḥanan the first-born, the second Yehoyaqim, the third Tsiḏqiyahu, the fourth Shallum. [16] And the sons of Yehoyaqim: Yeḵonyah his son and Tsiḏqiyah his son.

readings.title: The Remnant's Endurance
readings.subtitle: The Preservation of the Elohim Family Name
readings.text: [17] And the sons of Yeḵonyah the captive: She’alti’ĕl his son, [18] and Malkiram, and Peḏayah, and Shenatstsar, Yeqamyah, Hoshama, and Neḏaḇyah. [19] And the sons of Peḏayah: Zerubbaḇel and Shim’i. The sons of Zerubbaḇel: Meshullam, and Ḥananyah, and Shelomith their sister, [20] and Ḥashuḇah, and Ohel, and Bereḵyah, and Ḥasaḏyah, Yushaḇ-Ḥeseḏ, five. [21] And the sons of Ḥananyah: Pelatyah and Yeshayah, the sons of Rephayah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Oḇaḏyah, the sons of Sheḵanyah. [22] And the son of Sheḵanyah: Shemayah. The sons of Shemayah: Ḥattush, and Yiġ’al, and Bariyaḥ, and Ne’aryah, and Shaphat, six. [23] And the sons of Ne’aryah: Elyo’ĕynai, and Ḥizqiyah, and Azriqam, three. [24] And the sons of Elyo’ĕynai: Hoḏavyah, and Elyashiḇ, and Pelayah, and Aqquḇ, and Yoḥanan, and Delayah, and Anani, seven.

readings.title: The Aleph-Tav Guarantee
readings.subtitle: The Sweet Singer's Revelation of the Branch
readings.text: [2 Samuel 23:1] And these are the last words of Daviḏ, the saying of Daviḏ son of Yishai, the saying of the man raised above, the anointed of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya’aqoḇ, and the sweet singer of Yisra’ĕl: [2] “The Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken through me, And <dn>His</dn> word is on my tongue. [3] “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl said, The Rock of Yisra’ĕl spoke to me, <dq>‘One who rules over man righteously,</dq> [4] <dq>“Who rules in the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn>, Is like the light of the morning when the sun rises, A morning without clouds, Tender grass from the earth From sunshine, from rain.’</dq> [5] “For is not my house so with <dn>את</dn> <dn>Ĕl</dn>? For <dn>He</dn> has made an everlasting covenant with me, Ordered in all matters, and guarded. For all my deliverance and all desire, Shall <dn>He</dn> not make it send forth a Branch? [6] “But the worthless are all as thorns thrust away, For they are not taken with hands, [7] “But the man who touches them Uses iron or the shaft of a spear, And with fire they are burned up in their place.”

readings.title: The First Three
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Instruments of Deliverance
readings.text: [8] These are the names of the mighty men whom Daviḏ had: Yoshĕḇ-Bassheḇeth the Taḥkemonite, chief among the officers, he was Aḏino the Etsnite, for eight hundred slain at one time. [9] And after him was El’azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, one of the three mighty men with <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ when they taunted the Philistines who were gathered there for battle, and the men of Yisra’ĕl had gone up. [10] He arose and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary, but his hand clung to the sword, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought about a great deliverance that day. And the people returned after him only to plunder. [11] And after him was Shammah son of Agĕ the Hararite. And the Philistines had gathered into a company where there was a plot of ground covered with lentils, and the people fled from the Philistines. [12] But he took his stand in the middle of the field, and delivered it, and struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> wrought a great deliverance.

readings.title: The Libation of Trust
readings.subtitle: A Sacrifice of Pure Devotion
readings.text: [13] And three of the thirty chief men went down at harvest time and came to Daviḏ at the cave of Aḏullam, while the army of Philistines encamped in the Valley of Repha’im. [14] And Daviḏ was then in the stronghold, while a watch-post of the Philistines was then in Bĕyth Leḥem. [15] And Daviḏ longed and said, “Oh that someone would give me a drink of the water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!” [16] And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Daviḏ. But he would not drink it, but poured it out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] And he said, “Far be it from me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to do this – the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives!” So he would not drink it. This is what the three mighty men did.

readings.title: The Ordered Leadership
readings.subtitle: Deeds of the High-Capacity Servants
readings.text: [18] And Aḇishai the brother of Yo’aḇ, son of Tseruyah, was chief of another three. And he lifted <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred men whom he slew, and had a name among these three. [19] Was he not the most esteemed of three? And he became their commander, but he did not come to the first three. [20] And Benayahu was the son of Yehoyaḏa, son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, great in deeds. He struck <dn>את</dn> two lion-like men of Mo’aḇ. And he went down and struck <dn>את</dn> a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day. [21] And he struck <dn>את</dn> a Mitsrian, an impressive man. And the Mitsrian had a spear in his hand, so he went down to him with a staff, wrested <dn>את</dn> the spear out of the Mitsrian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear. [22] This is what Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa did, and had a name among three mighty men. [23] He was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come to the first three. And Daviḏ set <dn>את</dn> him over his guard.

readings.title: The Thirty-Seven Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: The Foundation of the King's Army
readings.text: [24] Asah’ĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ was one of the thirty; Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem, [25] Shammah the Ḥaroḏite, Eliqa the Ḥaroḏite, [26] Ḥelets the Paltite, Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqovite, [27] Aḇi’ezer the Anethothite, Meḇunnai the Ḥushathite, [28] Tsalmon the Aḥoḥite, Maharai the Netophathite, [29] Ḥĕleḏ son of Ba’anah the Netophathite, Ittai son of Riḇai from Giḇ’ah of the children of Binyamin, [30] Benayahu the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the wadis of Ga’ash, [31] Aḇi-Alḇon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barḥumite, [32] Elyaḥba the Sha’albonite of the sons of Yashĕn, Yehonathan, [33] Shammah the Hararite, Aḥyam son of Sharar the Hararite, [34] Eliphelet son of Aḥasbai, son of the Ma’aḵathite, Eliyam son of Aḥithophel the Gilonite, [35] Ḥetsrai the Karmelite, Pa’arai the Arbite, [36] Yiġ’al son of Nathan of Tsoḇah, Bani the Gaḏite, [37] Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Be’ĕrothite, armour-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah, [38] Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite, [39] and Uriyah the Ḥittite – thirty-seven in all.

readings.title: The Authorization of the Rightful Ruler
readings.subtitle: The Covenant Before YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 11:1] And all Yisra’ĕl came together to Daviḏ at Ḥeḇron, saying, “See, we are your bone and your flesh. [2] “Also, in time past, even when Sha’ul was sovereign, you were the one who led Yisra’ĕl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> said to you, <dq>‘Shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, and be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.’</dq> ” [3] So all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Daviḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ sovereign over Yisra’ĕl, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by Shemu’ĕl.

readings.title: Capturing the Epicenter
readings.subtitle: Establishing the City of Daviḏ
readings.text: [4] And Daviḏ and all Yisra’ĕl went to Yerushalayim, which is Yeḇus, where the Yeḇusites were, the inhabitants of the land. [5] And the inhabitants of Yeḇus said to Daviḏ, “You do not come in here.” But Daviḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, the City of Daviḏ. [6] And Daviḏ said, “Whoever strikes the Yeḇusites first becomes chief and commander.” And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah went up first, and became chief. [7] And Daviḏ dwelt in the stronghold, so they called it the City of Daviḏ. [8] And he built <dn>את</dn> the city around it, from Millo round about, and Yo’aḇ revived <dn>את</dn> the rest of the city. [9] And Daviḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts was with <dn>את</dn> him.

readings.title: The First Edge of the Sword
readings.subtitle: Guarding the Authorized Inheritance
readings.text: [10] And these were the heads of the mighty men whom Daviḏ had, who strengthened themselves with <dn>את</dn> him in his reign, with <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl, to set him up to reign over Yisra’ĕl, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] And this is the number of the mighty men whom Daviḏ had: Yashoḇ’am son of a Ḥaḵmonite, chief of the thirty. He had lifted up <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred, slain at one time. [12] And after him was El’azar son of Doḏo, the Aḥoḥite, who was one of the three mighty men. [13] He was with <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ at Pasdammim, and the Philistines were gathered there for battle, and a portion of the field was filled with barley, and the people had fled before the Philistines. [14] But they took their stand in the midst of that field, and delivered it, and struck <dn>את</dn> the Philistines. Thus <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saved them by a great deliverance.

readings.title: The Economy of Blood and Water
readings.subtitle: The Devotion of the Three
readings.text: [15] And three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to Daviḏ, into the cave of Aḏullam, while the army of the Philistines encamped in the Valley of Repha’im. [16] And Daviḏ was then in the stronghold, and the watch-post of the Philistines was then in Bĕyth Leḥem. [17] And Daviḏ longed and said, “Oh, that someone would give me a drink of water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem, which is by the gate!” [18] And the three broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water from the well of Bĕyth Leḥem that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Daviḏ. But Daviḏ would not drink it, but poured it out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [19] And he said, “Far be it from me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who have risked their lives? For at the risk of their lives they brought it.” And he would not drink it. This is what the three mighty men did.

readings.title: The Hierarchy of Power
readings.subtitle: The Defenders of the Court
readings.text: [20] And Aḇishai the brother of Yo’aḇ was chief of another three. And he had lifted up <dn>את</dn> his spear against three hundred men, who were slain, and won a name among the three. [21] Of the three he was more esteemed than the other two men, so he became their head. However he did not come to the first three. [22] Benayah was the son of Yehoyaḏa, the son of a brave man from Qaḇtse’ĕl, who had done many deeds. He struck <dn>את</dn> two lion-like Mo’aḇites. He also went down and struck <dn>את</dn> a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day. [23] And he struck <dn>את</dn> a Mitsrian, a man of great height, five cubits tall. And in the Mitsrian’s hand was a spear like a weaver’s beam, and he went down to him with a staff and wrenched <dn>את</dn> the spear out of the Mitsrian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear. [24] This is what Benayahu son of Yehoyaḏa did, and won a name among the three mighty men. [25] See, he was more esteemed than the thirty, but he did not come to the first three. And Daviḏ set <dn>את</dn> him over his court.

readings.title: The Fullness of the Mighty Men
readings.subtitle: The Legions of the Anointed
readings.text: [26] And the mighty men of the armies were Asah’ĕl the brother of Yo’aḇ, Elḥanan son of Doḏo of Bĕyth Leḥem, [27] Shammoth the Harorite, Ḥĕlets the Pelonite, [28] Ira son of Iqqĕsh the Teqovite, Aḇi’ezer the Anathothite, [29] Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite, Ilai the Aḥoḥite, [30] Maharai the Netophathite, Ḥĕleḏ son of Ba’anah the Netophathite, [31] Ithai son of Riḇai of Giḇ’ah, of the children of Binyamin, Benayah the Pirathonite, [32] Ḥurai of the wadis of Ga’ash, Aḇi’ĕl the Arbathite, [33] Azmaveth the Baḥarumite, Elyaḥba the Sha’albonite, [34] the sons of Hashĕm the Gizonite, Yonathan son of Shaġĕ the Hararite, [35] Aḥyam son of Saḵar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur, [36] Ḥĕpher the Mekĕrathite, Aḥiyah the Pelonite, [37] Ḥetsro the Karmelite, Na’arai son of Ezbai, [38] Yo’ĕl the brother of Nathan, Miḇḥar son of Haġri, [39] Tseleq the Ammonite, Naḥarai the Bĕrothite (the armour-bearer of Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah), [40] Ira the Yithrite, Garĕḇ the Yithrite, [41] Uriyah the Ḥittite, Zaḇaḏ son of Aḥlai, [42] Aḏina son of Shiza the Re’uḇĕnite, the head of the Re’uḇĕnites, and thirty with <dn>את</dn> him, [43] Ḥanan son of Ma’aḵah, and Yoshaphat the Mithnite, [44] Uzziya the Ashterathite, Shama and Ye’i’ĕl the sons of Ḥotham the Aro’ĕrite, [45] Yeḏiya’ĕl son of Shimri, and Yoḥa his brother, the Titsite, [46] Eli’ĕl the Maḥavite, and Yeriḇai and Yoshavyah the sons of Elna’am, Yithmah the Mo’aḇite, [47] Eli’ĕl, and Oḇĕḏ, and Ya’asi’ĕl of Metsoḇayah.
